Hackers Publish Malicious Python Package Mimicking Legitimate Parsimonious Parser

Cyber Security News
2026-06-05 1 use case 0 techniques 1 kill-chain phase detected

A deceptive Python package quietly made its way into the PyPI repository, putting thousands of developers at risk before it was caught and removed. The package, named &#8220;parsimonius,&#8221; was crafted to look almost identical to the widely used &#8220;parsimonious&#8221; library, a popular Python tool for building expression grammar parsers. The single missing letter was no [&#8230;] The post Hackers Publish Malicious Python Package Mimicking Legitimate Parsimonious Parser appeared first on Cyber Security News .

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089") or SHA1 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089") or MD5 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089") or SHA1 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089") or MD5 in~ ("a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

IronWorm and New Miasma Worm Variant Hit npm in Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker NewsStepSecurity
2026-06-05 15 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

[LLM] Installation of compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI versions 1.4.1-1.4.3 Delivery High
Detects pip installation of the three malicious durabletask SDK versions (1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) published to PyPI on 2026-05-19. Hits every CI runner, build host, or developer workstation that pulled the trojanised release; pin to 1.4.0 and treat any match as compromised. Rationale: Pins on the three article-named malicious versions of the official 400k-DL/month durabletask package, only legitimate channel is pip install referencing one of those version strings. Hashes (069ac1dc... / 7d80b3ef... / aeaf583e...) cross-referenced via StepSecurity public run analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1195.002

[LLM] Python urlretrieve download of rope.pyz from check.git-service.com to /tmp/managed.pyz Installation High
Catches the 14-line dropper executing at `import durabletask` time: a Python process performs an HTTPS GET to check.git-service.com/rope.pyz and writes the response to /tmp/managed.pyz. Highly specific to the TeamPCP rope.pyz framework — the URL path /rope.pyz and target filename /tmp/managed.pyz are both attacker-chosen literals. Rationale: Three article-grounded literals correlated: process is python*, destination is `check.git-service.com` (or its 160.119.64.3 / 83.142.209.194 IPs), and the write target is `/tmp/managed.pyz`. Any pair is suspicious; all three is the dropper. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let C2 = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","git-service.com"]);
let C2IP = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
let Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (C2) or RemoteIP in (C2IP);
let Drop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > TimeRange
    | where FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName =~ "managed.pyz"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14");
union Net, Drop
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Python-urllib","python-requests","python3")
         or Url has "rope.pyz"
    | where HttpHostName has_any (C2) or DstIpAddr in (C2IP) or Url has_any (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, HttpHostName, Url, DstIpAddr;
let Drop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
    | where TargetFilePath has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union Net, Drop
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] python3 import durabletask spawning detached /tmp/managed.pyz collector swarm Installation High
Detects the rope.pyz post-import behaviour: a single `python3 -c "import durabletask"` parent spawning multiple `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` children, each detached via start_new_session=True. Hunting for the parent→child binary pair `/tmp/managed.pyz` is essentially zero-FP — that path was attacker-chosen specifically to look bland. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates the process tree: PID 2380/2404/2430/2432 all `python3 /tmp/managed.pyz` from a single parent. The cmdline literal `/tmp/managed.pyz` + python parent is article-specific and not a generic LOLBin pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.003

| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"

          by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId
| where ChildPids >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")

          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId
| where ChildPids >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor.service persistence via systemctl --user daemon-reload from python parent Installation High
rope.pyz installs a fake systemd user unit named pgsql-monitor.service then issues `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. Detects the cmdline `systemctl --user daemon-reload` when spawned by python3 — and any creation of a unit file named pgsql-monitor.service. Non-obvious persistence path: user-scope (not system) so root isn't needed. Rationale: Two article-specific literals: the deliberately bland service name `pgsql-monitor.service` and the `systemctl --user daemon-reload` cmdline spawned by python3. Neither is a normal admin operation in a CI runner or microservice host. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546

    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Source = "file";

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GPG batch passphrase 'anon' + gh auth token credential harvesting from python parent Actions on Objectives High
rope.pyz collectors invoke `gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt` (a literal, hard-coded passphrase) and `gh auth token` / `gh auth status --show-token` from a python3 parent. The cmdline `--passphrase anon` is essentially unique to this campaign; `gh auth token` from a non-shell parent (python3) is the second high-fidelity tell. Rationale: `--passphrase anon` is a literal attacker-chosen passphrase essentially unique to rope.pyz; `gh auth token` parented by python3 is unusual everywhere (gh is interactive CLI). Article enumerates both for every managed.pyz child. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (FileName =~ "gpg" and ProcessCommandLine has "--batch" and ProcessCommandLine has "--passphrase" and ProcessCommandLine has " anon" and ProcessCommandLine has "--decrypt")
   or (FileName =~ "gh" and (ProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or ProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (TargetProcessName has "gpg" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--batch" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--passphrase" and TargetProcessCommandLine has " anon" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--decrypt")
   or (TargetProcessName has "gh" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "auth token" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "auth status --show-token"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GPG --passphrase anon + gh auth token from Python (rope.pyz Credential Theft)
id: 6b1f2a18-3d44-4f10-93c6-7f3a9b8e1f05
description: Detects the rope.pyz credential collectors invoking gpg --batch --passphrase anon --decrypt and gh auth token/status --show-token from a python3 parent.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/ironworm-and-new-miasma-worm-variant.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.t1555
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent_python:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/python3.14'
  gpg_anon:
    Image|endswith: '/gpg'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '--batch'
      - '--passphrase anon'
      - '--decrypt'
  gh_token:
    Image|endswith: '/gh'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'auth token'
      - 'auth status --show-token'
  condition: parent_python and (gpg_anon or gh_token)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.parent.name:(python OR python3 OR python3.14) ((@process.name:gpg @process.command_line:(*--batch* *--passphrase\ anon* *--decrypt*)) OR (@process.name:gh @process.command_line:(*"auth token"* OR *"auth status --show-token"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?(\.14)?)$/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/gpg$/i AND regex("--batch.*--passphrase\\s+anon.*--decrypt", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/\/gh$/i AND regex("auth\\s+(token|status\\s+--show-token)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.14") ((Processes.process_name="gpg" AND Processes.process="*--batch*--passphrase*anon*--decrypt*") OR (Processes.process_name="gh" AND (Processes.process="*auth token*" OR Processes.process="*auth status --show-token*"))) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] DNS / connection to TeamPCP secondary C2 m-kosche.com Command & Control High
Catches any host resolving or connecting to the TeamPCP infrastructure: primary C2 git-service.com / check.git-service.com (160.119.64.3) and Mini Shai-Hulud secondary C2 m-kosche.com / t.m-kosche.com (83.142.209.194). The secondary C2 is the cross-campaign tie linking this incident to TanStack, LiteLLM, Mistral, and @antv compromises. Rationale: Four article-listed FQDNs + two attacker-controlled IPs (NameSilo / PrivacyGuardian-registered git-service.com on 2026-05-16, HostUS AS7489 hosting). Secondary C2 m-kosche.com is the cross-campaign tie to Mini Shai-Hulud (TanStack/LiteLLM/Mistral/@antv) which makes the m-kosche match particularly high-fidelity. CloudWatch left empty because VPC Flow Log fields (srcAddr/dstAddr) aren't on the CloudTrail field whitelist this pipeline accepts. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let BadDomains = dynamic(["m-kosche.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com","check.git-service.com"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains) or RemoteIP in (BadIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let TimeRange = ago(30d);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["m-kosche.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com","check.git-service.com"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DnsQuery, Channel = "DNS", Vendor = EventVendor, Product = EventProduct
),
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DstHostname has_any (BadDomains) or DstIpAddr in (BadIPs) or Url has_any (BadDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, tostring(DstIpAddr)), Channel = "Network", Vendor = EventVendor, Product = EventProduct
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > TimeRange
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains) or DestinationIP in (BadIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, tostring(DestinationIP)), Channel = "CSL", Vendor = DeviceVendor, Product = DeviceProduct
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand / kubectl exec lateral movement from compromised CI runtime Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the rope.pyz lateral-movement phase: `kubectl version --client` (recon) and `kubectl exec` (lateral) spawned by python3, plus AWS SSM SendCommand / StartSession originating from an EC2 / CI identity that was active around the time managed.pyz fired. Article calls out AWS SSM and kubectl exec specifically as the two propagation channels. Rationale: Three article-specific commands: `kubectl version --client` (article's exact K8s recon string), `kubectl exec` (article's exact lateral movement primitive), and `aws ssm send-command/start-session` (the article's named AWS lateral channel). All three are valid admin operations in isolation — the python3 parent context is what makes the signal. The CloudTrail half adds tenant-side visibility independent of EDR coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1609 T1018
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (FileName =~ "kubectl" and (ProcessCommandLine has "version --client" or ProcessCommandLine has " exec "))
   or (FileName =~ "aws" and (ProcessCommandLine has "ssm send-command" or ProcessCommandLine has "ssm start-session"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","python3.14")
| where (TargetProcessName has "kubectl" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "version --client" or TargetProcessCommandLine has " exec "))
   or (TargetProcessName has "aws" and (TargetProcessCommandLine has "ssm send-command" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "ssm start-session"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.parent.name:(python OR python3 OR python3.14) ((@process.name:kubectl @process.command_line:(*"version --client"* OR *" exec "*)) OR (@process.name:aws @process.command_line:(*"ssm send-command"* OR *"ssm start-session"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?(\.14)?)$/i
| (ImageFileName=/\/kubectl$/i AND regex("version\\s+--client|\\sexec\\s", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/\/aws$/i AND regex("ssm\\s+(send-command|start-session)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, awsRegion, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.attributes.mfaAuthenticated, requestParameters.instanceIds.0, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target, userAgent
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["SendCommand","StartSession","ResumeSession"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and (userAgent like /Boto3/ or userAgent like /python-requests/ or userAgent like /aws-cli/)
      and userIdentity.type in ["AssumedRole","IAMUser","Federated"]
| sort @timestamp desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.14") (Processes.process_name="kubectl" OR Processes.process_name="aws") (Processes.process="*kubectl*exec*" OR Processes.process="*kubectl version --client*" OR Processes.process="*ssm send-command*" OR Processes.process="*ssm start-session*") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

[LLM] HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) Exploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Shopper Admin Team Settings / Livewire Endpoint Access (CVE-2026-47744)
id: 9f6c5d22-2e4f-4b3a-9d6e-7c8a2b9d4e10
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests to Shopper admin panel team-settings routes (Settings/Team/Index, Settings/Team/RolePermission) and their underlying Livewire endpoints, which were the abuse path for CVE-2026-47744 (authorization bypass + RBAC privilege escalation) in shopper/framework versions below 2.8.0.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:

    - attack.t1068
    - attack.t1078.003
    - cve.2026.47744
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_path:
        cs-uri-stem|contains:
            - 'settings/team'
            - 'settings.team.index'
            - 'settings.team.role-permission'
            - 'settings.team.rolepermission'
            - '/livewire/update'
            - '/livewire/message/settings.team'
    condition: selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate Shopper administrators managing roles in the admin panel
    - Internal QA/staging exercising the team settings page
level: medium
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:azure.app_services) (@http.url_details.path:(*settings/team* OR *settings.team.index* OR *settings.team.role-permission* OR *settings.team.rolePermission*) OR @http.url_details.path:(*/livewire/update* OR */livewire/message/settings.team*)) AND @http.method:(POST OR PUT OR PATCH)
# log group: /aws/applicationelb (or /aws/cloudfront/access-logs, /aws/wafv2) — point at whichever fronts the Shopper admin panel
fields @timestamp, request_url, request_verb, elb_status_code, client_ip, user_agent, target_processing_time
| filter (request_url like /settings\/team/ 
         or request_url like /settings\.team\.index/ 
         or request_url like /settings\.team\.role-?permission/i
         or request_url like /\/livewire\/(update|message\/settings\.team)/)
      and request_verb in ["POST","PUT","PATCH"]
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

        | where SHA256 in~ ("174086534a2de730058465a4a4e231ce3778ab17ebebfd7f62b3bf9750bc7bdb", "e3541caf708c075f0bb22fc68b03acd8457fea7cf0732ea935b1eb016d1c7721", "8046735d354814bf9ef9a053cb9cad8cfec261f2", "8462f61e68b37d220eab2462b3cbcec8") or SHA1 in~ ("174086534a2de730058465a4a4e231ce3778ab17ebebfd7f62b3bf9750bc7bdb", "e3541caf708c075f0bb22fc68b03acd8457fea7cf0732ea935b1eb016d1c7721", "8046735d354814bf9ef9a053cb9cad8cfec261f2", "8462f61e68b37d220eab2462b3cbcec8") or MD5 in~ ("174086534a2de730058465a4a4e231ce3778ab17ebebfd7f62b3bf9750bc7bdb", "e3541caf708c075f0bb22fc68b03acd8457fea7cf0732ea935b1eb016d1c7721", "8046735d354814bf9ef9a053cb9cad8cfec261f2", "8462f61e68b37d220eab2462b3cbcec8")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["174086534a2de730058465a4a4e231ce3778ab17ebebfd7f62b3bf9750bc7bdb", "e3541caf708c075f0bb22fc68b03acd8457fea7cf0732ea935b1eb016d1c7721", "8046735d354814bf9ef9a053cb9cad8cfec261f2", "8462f61e68b37d220eab2462b3cbcec8"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2021-27137", "CVE-2015-2051", "CVE-2022-35914", "CVE-2016-15047", "CVE-2025-34054")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

union

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Internet-exposed unpatched SolarWinds Serv-U servers (CVE-2026-28318 exposure hunt) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 — inbound POST with Content-Encoding: deflate
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] SolarWinds Serv-U service crash / abnormal restart loop (CVE-2026-28318 impact) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 — inbound POST with Content-Encoding: deflate Delivery High
Detects the network signature of the CVE-2026-28318 DoS exploit: unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing a 'Content-Encoding: deflate' header directed at the Serv-U MFT/FTP web listener. SolarWinds explicitly states the vulnerable Serv-U service does not require this header for any legitimate function, so its presence on a POST to the Serv-U listener is high-fidelity for exploit attempts. Rationale: Vendor advisory states the vulnerable Serv-U service does not require Content-Encoding for any function and recommends WAFs block POSTs containing this header — making the POST+deflate combination a near-zero-FP signature. Header inspection requires WAF/web-tier visibility; Defender XDR DeviceNetworkEvents does not surface HTTP headers, so the Defender query pivots to inbound-connection + service-restart correlation instead. Corroborated against NVD CVE-2026-28318 entry which restates the exact deflate POST condition. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318 • https://documentation.solarwinds.com/en/success_center/servu/content/release_notes/servu_15-5-4_release_notes.htm • https://www.csa.gov.sg/alerts-and-advisories/alerts/al-2026-018/
ATT&CKT1190 T1499.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender DeviceNetworkEvents does not expose HTTP request headers, so we pivot to the
// Serv-U process accepting inbound connections clustered immediately before a service
// restart event (paired with UC "Serv-U service crash"). Best-effort surface.
let WindowMin = 5m;
let ServUInbound =
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess","ListeningConnectionCreated")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Serv-U.exe"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let ServURestart =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "Serv-U.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "services.exe"
    | project ProcTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine;
ServUInbound
| join kind=inner ServURestart on DeviceId
| where ProcTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + WindowMin)
| summarize InboundConnections = count(), DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP), SampleRemoteIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 10), FirstNet = min(NetTime), FirstRestart = min(ProcTime) by DeviceId, DeviceName
| where InboundConnections >= 1
| order by FirstRestart desc
// CommonSecurityLog (WAF / reverse-proxy CEF) and W3CIISLog are the natural places
// a Content-Encoding header survives. RequestContext + DeviceCustomString fields on
// CEF carry headers depending on vendor; csUriQuery on IIS does not include them, so
// W3CIISLog catches the POST but the header check needs WAF or app-firewall.
let StartTime = ago(7d);
let WafSignal =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where (RequestContext has "content-encoding: deflate")
         or (DeviceCustomString1 has "deflate") or (DeviceCustomString2 has "deflate")
         or (DeviceCustomString3 has "deflate") or (DeviceCustomString4 has "deflate")
         or (Message has "Content-Encoding: deflate")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIP = SourceIP, DstIP = DestinationIP, DstPort = DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestContext, Message;
let IISSignal =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > StartTime
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where sPort in ("443","80","8443")
    | where csUriStem has_any ("/Web Client","/WebClient","/ServUWeb","/servu")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIP = cIp, DstIP = Computer, DstPort = sPort, RequestURL = csUriStem, DeviceVendor = "Microsoft", DeviceProduct = "IIS", RequestContext = "", Message = strcat(csMethod, " ", csUriStem);
union WafSignal, IISSignal
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleURLs = make_set(RequestURL, 5) by SrcIP, DstIP, DstPort, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by HitCount desc
title: SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 Exploit Attempt - POST with Content-Encoding deflate
id: 8f9d7b1c-2a3e-4b6d-9e1f-0c5a7d2e9b4f
status: experimental
description: Detects unauthenticated POST requests containing a Content-Encoding deflate header that exploit CVE-2026-28318 to crash the SolarWinds Serv-U MFT/FTP service.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-hackers-now-exploit-solarwinds-serv-u-flaw-to-crash-servers/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318
  - https://documentation.solarwinds.com/en/success_center/servu/content/release_notes/servu_15-5-4_release_notes.htm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1499.003
  - cve.2026.28318
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: POST
  selection_header:
    cs-content-encoding|contains: deflate
  condition: selection_method and selection_header
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate clients that erroneously set Content-Encoding deflate on POSTs (rare; Serv-U does not require this header for any function per vendor advisory)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:cloudfront OR source:azure.applicationgateway OR source:f5 OR source:cloudflare) @http.method:POST (@http.request_headers.content-encoding:deflate OR @http.request_headers.Content-Encoding:deflate OR "Content-Encoding: deflate")
WEB
`summariesonly` is non-applicable for raw header detection; use raw access-log search.
(sourcetype IN ("iis:access","nginx:access","apache:access","waf:*","cisco:wsa","f5:asm") OR tag=web)
  http_method=POST
  ("Content-Encoding: deflate" OR "Content-Encoding:deflate" OR "content-encoding: deflate")
| eval likely_servu = if(match(url, "(?i)/Web%20Client|/?ServUWeb|/?WebClient|/?servu") OR dest_port IN ("443","80","8443"), 1, 0)
| stats count, min(_time) AS firstSeen, max(_time) AS lastSeen, values(url) AS urls, values(http_user_agent) AS user_agents, dc(src) AS distinct_sources BY src, dest, dest_port, likely_servu
| where count >= 1
| sort - count
[LLM] SolarWinds Serv-U service crash / abnormal restart loop (CVE-2026-28318 impact) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the impact stage of CVE-2026-28318 exploitation: Serv-U.exe (Windows) or serv-u systemd unit (Linux) terminating unexpectedly and being restarted by services.exe / systemd, particularly in clusters (multiple restarts in a short window). This is the observable evidence that a successful or attempted DoS exploit reached the vulnerable Serv-U parser. Rationale: Article and vendor advisory both state the exploit causes the Serv-U service to crash — services.exe will then auto-restart it on Windows, producing a tight restart cluster (3+ restarts in <30 min) that is not seen during normal operation. EventID 7031/7034 with 'Serv-U' in the message is the canonical Windows signal. Threshold tuned to reduce single-restart noise from planned maintenance. Corroborated via NVD CVE-2026-28318 and SolarWinds Serv-U 15.5.4 release notes. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318 • https://documentation.solarwinds.com/en/success_center/servu/content/release_notes/servu_15-5-4_release_notes.htm
ATT&CKT1499 T1499.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TightWindow = 30m;
let RestartFloor = 3;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "Serv-U.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "services.exe"
| summarize RestartCount = count(),
            FirstRestart = min(Timestamp),
            LastRestart = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
         by DeviceId, DeviceName
| extend WindowMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastRestart, FirstRestart)
| where RestartCount >= RestartFloor and WindowMin <= 30
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("ServiceInstalled","WdacAuditPolicyChanged") or AdditionalFields has "Serv-U"
    | project DeviceId, AuditEvtTime = Timestamp, AuditAction = ActionType
) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, RestartCount, WindowMin, FirstRestart, LastRestart, SampleCmd
| order by RestartCount desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ServUCrashes =
    Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventLog =~ "System"
    | where EventID in (7031, 7034)
    | where RenderedDescription has "Serv-U" or ParameterXml has "Serv-U"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, RenderedDescription;
let ServURestarts =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\Serv-U.exe"
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\services.exe"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine;
ServUCrashes
| union ServURestarts
| summarize EventCount = count(),
            FirstEvent = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastEvent = max(TimeGenerated),
            EventTypes = make_set(coalesce(tostring(EventID), "4688"))
         by Computer
| extend WindowMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastEvent, FirstEvent)
| where EventCount >= 2 and WindowMin <= 30
| order by EventCount desc
title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Unexpected Termination
id: 4b3c2e1d-7a9f-4d8b-b2c6-1f3e8a9d0c5b
status: experimental
description: Detects Windows Service Control Manager events reporting the Serv-U service terminating unexpectedly, consistent with CVE-2026-28318 DoS exploitation.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-hackers-now-exploit-solarwinds-serv-u-flaw-to-crash-servers/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1499
  - attack.t1499.003
  - cve.2026.28318
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: system
detection:
  selection:
    Provider_Name: 'Service Control Manager'
    EventID:
      - 7031
      - 7034
    param1|contains: 'Serv-U'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Planned Serv-U maintenance restarts performed manually
  - Underlying disk / OS resource pressure unrelated to the deflate POST exploit
level: high
(source:windows.system OR source:windows.security) (@EventID:7031 OR @EventID:7034 OR @EventID:4688) ("Serv-U" OR @Image:(*\\Serv-U.exe OR *\\serv-u.exe) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\Serv-U.exe OR *\\serv-u.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\Serv-U\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^services\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[count(as=RestartCount), min(@timestamp, as=FirstRestart), max(@timestamp, as=LastRestart)])
| WindowSec := (LastRestart - FirstRestart) / 1000
| RestartCount >= 3
| WindowSec <= 1800
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
// Windows Service Control Manager crash events for Serv-U
(index=wineventlog OR index=winevent) source="WinEventLog:System"
  EventCode IN (7031, 7034)
  (Message="*Serv-U*" OR param1="*Serv-U*" OR ServiceName="*Serv-U*")
| stats count AS CrashCount, min(_time) AS firstCrash, max(_time) AS lastCrash, values(EventCode) AS event_codes, values(Message) AS sample_messages BY host
| eval window_minutes = round((lastCrash - firstCrash) / 60, 1)
| where CrashCount >= 2 OR (CrashCount >= 1 AND window_minutes <= 30)
| sort - CrashCount

// Complementary CIM Endpoint.Processes pivot for Serv-U spawned by services.exe in tight cluster
| append [
  | tstats summariesonly=t count AS RestartCount, min(_time) AS firstRestart, max(_time) AS lastRestart FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.process_name="Serv-U.exe" Processes.parent_process_name="services.exe" BY Processes.dest
  | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
  | rename dest AS host
  | where RestartCount >= 3 AND (lastRestart - firstRestart) <= 1800
]
// Windows Service Control Manager crash events for Serv-U
(index=wineventlog OR index=winevent) source="WinEventLog:System"
  EventCode IN (7031, 7034)
  (Message="*Serv-U*" OR param1="*Serv-U*" OR ServiceName="*Serv-U*")
| stats count AS CrashCount, min(_time) AS firstCrash, max(_time) AS lastCrash, values(EventCode) AS event_codes, values(Message) AS sample_messages BY host
| eval window_minutes = round((lastCrash - firstCrash) / 60, 1)
| where CrashCount >= 2 OR (CrashCount >= 1 AND window_minutes <= 30)
| sort - CrashCount

// Complementary CIM Endpoint.Processes pivot for Serv-U spawned by services.exe in tight cluster
| append [
  | tstats summariesonly=false count AS RestartCount, min(_time) AS firstRestart, max(_time) AS lastRestart FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.process_name="Serv-U.exe" Processes.parent_process_name="services.exe" BY Processes.dest
  | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
  | rename dest AS host
  | where RestartCount >= 3 AND (lastRestart - firstRestart) <= 1800
]
[LLM] Internet-exposed unpatched SolarWinds Serv-U servers (CVE-2026-28318 exposure hunt) Reconnaissance High
Proactive exposure hunt for Serv-U installations vulnerable to CVE-2026-28318 — any Serv-U build older than 15.5.4 Hotfix 1, especially those marked Internet-facing. Article cites 12,000+ Shodan-exposed instances and CISA's KEV catalog mandate to patch by June 19; this UC surfaces our owned vulnerable footprint before attackers reach it. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out 12,000+ Internet-exposed Serv-U instances and the BOD 22-01 patch deadline of 2026-06-19 for federal agencies — making our own exposed/unpatched Serv-U footprint the highest-leverage signal to surface before exploitation. MDVM TVM tables provide authoritative CVE-to-asset mapping; IsInternetFacing flag prioritises the BOD-relevant subset. Sigma/Datadog/LogScale/CloudWatch left empty because TVM is not single-event-shape and ships only via MDVM (not Falcon Spotlight FDR or CloudTrail). Corroborated via NVD and SolarWinds vendor release notes for the 15.5.4 Hotfix 1 patch line. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-28318 • https://documentation.solarwinds.com/en/success_center/servu/content/release_notes/servu_15-5-4_release_notes.htm • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1190

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

ImFileEvent

| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")

            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)

| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) Exploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1

[LLM] ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) Command & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py

[LLM] AgentPSD — Python reverse shell fallback persistence on Linux / NAS hosts Installation Medium
Detects the AgentPSD fallback persistence channel Volexity recovered from a Synology NAS: a Python-based reverse shell that imports socket/subprocess/pty and pipes /bin/sh I/O over a TCP socket to a UNC5221 C2 domain. Linux MDE / auditd / ASIM ImProcessCreate is the target telemetry; Windows hosts are out of scope for this UC. Rationale: Article explicitly names AgentPSD as a Python-based reverse shell deployed as fallback persistence on a Synology NAS after Brickstorm was identified. The signature targets the canonical Python reverse-shell pattern (import socket/subprocess/pty + shell redirection) constrained to Linux/NAS hosts so it doesn't collide with legitimate developer Python usage on Windows endpoints. Schema: DeviceProcessEvents uses FileName/ProcessCommandLine; ImProcessCreate uses ActingProcessName/ActingProcessCommandLine/TargetProcessCommandLine (verified against the canonical schemas above). Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/category/threat-research/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1071.001 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName matches regex @"^python[0-9\.]*$"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "import"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("socket.socket","subprocess.call","subprocess.Popen","pty.spawn","os.dup2","/bin/sh","/bin/bash","connect((")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DvcOs has_any ("Linux","BSD","Unix","Synology","DSM")
     or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(^|/)python[0-9\.]*$"
     or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(^|/)python[0-9\.]*$"
| extend CmdLine = coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| where CmdLine has "import"
| where CmdLine has_any ("socket.socket","subprocess.call","subprocess.Popen","pty.spawn","os.dup2","/bin/sh","/bin/bash","connect((")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Python Reverse Shell Pattern (AgentPSD / UNC5221 fallback)
id: c1d39e44-8ae2-4d2a-8df7-7c9c4d3f8c61
description: Detects python invocations whose command line imports socket / subprocess / pty together with a shell or fd-redirection primitive (os.dup2 / pty.spawn / /bin/sh) — the AgentPSD fallback reverse-shell shape Volexity attributes to UNC5221.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-apt-deploys-new-malware-to-keep-access-to-hacked-networks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|re: '(^|/)python[0-9.]*$'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'import'
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - 'socket.socket'
      - 'subprocess.call'
      - 'subprocess.Popen'
      - 'pty.spawn'
      - 'os.dup2'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/bash'
      - 'connect(('
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(python OR python2 OR python3) @process.command_line:(*"import socket"* OR *"socket.socket"* OR *"subprocess.call"* OR *"subprocess.Popen"* OR *"pty.spawn"* OR *"os.dup2"* OR *"/bin/sh"* OR *"/bin/bash"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/python[0-9\.]*$/i
| regex("import\\s+(socket|subprocess|pty|os)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(socket\\.socket|subprocess\\.(call|Popen)|pty\\.spawn|os\\.dup2|/bin/(sh|bash)|connect\\(\\()", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
