| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python2","python3","python3.6","python3.7","python3.8","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11") AND Processes.process="*import*" AND (Processes.process="*socket.socket*" OR Processes.process="*subprocess.call*" OR Processes.process="*subprocess.Popen*" OR Processes.process="*pty.spawn*" OR Processes.process="*os.dup2*" OR Processes.process="*/bin/sh*" OR Processes.process="*/bin/bash*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("python","python2","python3","python3.6","python3.7","python3.8","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11") AND Processes.process="*import*" AND (Processes.process="*socket.socket*" OR Processes.process="*subprocess.call*" OR Processes.process="*subprocess.Popen*" OR Processes.process="*pty.spawn*" OR Processes.process="*os.dup2*" OR Processes.process="*/bin/sh*" OR Processes.process="*/bin/bash*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Brickstorm SOCKS proxy: M365 sign-in originating from on-prem appliance IP (Conditional Access bypass) Command & Control Medium
Volexity assesses with high confidence that VerdantBamboo used Brickstorm's proxy feature on the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance to tunnel M365 authentication, so attacker sign-ins appear to originate from the victim's own egress IP and slip past Conditional Access policies that trust internal/named-location IPs. This UC hunts non-interactive or legacy-protocol M365 sign-ins coming from the public IP space of compromised edge appliances. Rationale: Article explicitly states the attacker used Brickstorm proxying so M365 auth blended in with legitimate network traffic and bypassed Conditional Access. CIDR list is a placeholder — the operator must replace with the actual public egress IPs of any Egnyte / pfSense / Synology / VPN concentrator under suspicion, ideally seeded from the asset inventory. Schema-checked: AADSignInEventsBeta uses Timestamp/AccountUpn/IPAddress; SigninLogs uses TimeGenerated/UserPrincipalName/IPAddress. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1006/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1556 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
let ApplianceEgressIPs = dynamic(["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.0/24"]);
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ResourceDisplayName has_any ("Office 365","Microsoft Graph","Exchange","SharePoint","OneDrive")
| where ipv4_is_in_any_range(IPAddress, ApplianceEgressIPs)
| where (IsInteractive == false) or ClientAppUsed in~ ("Exchange Web Services","IMAP4","POP3","Other clients","Authenticated SMTP")
| where ConditionalAccessStatus in~ ("success","notApplied")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, Country, AppDisplayName, ApplicationId, ClientAppUsed, IsInteractive, ConditionalAccessStatus, RiskState, UserAgent
| order by Timestamp desc
let ApplianceEgressIPs = dynamic(["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.0/24"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( SigninLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ResourceDisplayName has_any ("Office 365","Microsoft Graph","Exchange","SharePoint","OneDrive")
  | where ipv4_is_in_any_range(IPAddress, ApplianceEgressIPs)
  | where (IsInteractive == false) or ClientAppUsed in~ ("Exchange Web Services","IMAP4","POP3","Other clients","Authenticated SMTP")
  | where ConditionalAccessStatus in~ ("success","notApplied")
  | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UserDisplayName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, AppId, ClientAppUsed, IsInteractive, ConditionalAccessStatus, RiskState, UserAgent, ResultType
),
( AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ResourceDisplayName has_any ("Office 365","Microsoft Graph","Exchange","SharePoint","OneDrive")
  | where ipv4_is_in_any_range(IPAddress, ApplianceEgressIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UserDisplayName=Identity, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, AppId, ClientAppUsed, IsInteractive=false, ConditionalAccessStatus, RiskState=RiskLevelDuringSignIn, UserAgent="", ResultType
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" CIDR(@network.client.ip, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) (@properties.appDisplayName:("Office 365" OR "Microsoft Graph" OR Exchange*) OR @properties.clientAppUsed:("Exchange Web Services" OR IMAP4 OR POP3 OR "Other clients"))
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog
| (AppDisplayName=/office\s*365|microsoft\s*graph|exchange|sharepoint|onedrive/i)
| cidr("198.51.100.0/24", field=ClientIpAddress) OR cidr("203.0.113.0/24", field=ClientIpAddress)
| (IsInteractive="false" OR ClientAppUsed=/exchange\s*web\s*services|imap4|pop3|other\s*clients/i)
| groupBy([UserPrincipal, ClientIpAddress, AppDisplayName, ClientAppUsed], function=count())

[LLM] Unauthorized SSL VPN enablement / user provisioning on perimeter firewall Installation Medium
In the second intrusion, UNC5221 used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN on the victim's firewall, then connected back in to drop additional malware on a Synology NAS. This UC hunts firewall config-change events that turn on SSL VPN or add a VPN user from an unexpected admin source — both pfSense (Volexity confirmed the BSD Brickstorm variant lived on pfSense) and Fortinet/Palo Alto vendor strings are covered. Rationale: Article explicitly: 'attackers used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall'. The detection targets the actual config-change syslog/CEF lines that Fortinet, Palo Alto, Cisco and pfSense emit when SSL VPN is toggled on or a VPN user is added — Defender XDR has no visibility on firewall config so defender_kql is intentionally empty; falcon_logscale_query is empty for the same reason (Falcon FDR doesn't ship firewall syslog). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1133/ • https://www.volexity.com/blog/category/threat-research/
ATT&CKT1133 T1078 T1556
Data sourcesChange Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
union isfuzzy=true
( CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DeviceVendor in~ ("Fortinet","Palo Alto Networks","Cisco","Netgate","pfSense","SonicWall","Sophos")
  | where (Activity has_any ("ssl-vpn","sslvpn","SSL VPN","openvpn","vpn-user","vpn user"))
        or (Message has_any ("enable ssl-vpn","set status enable","ssl-vpn-settings","sslvpn settings","config vpn ssl settings","vpn-user-add"))
        or (DeviceEventClassID has_any ("vpnssl","ssl_vpn","sslvpn-cfg","config-change"))
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, Activity, Message, DeviceEventClassID
),
( Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Facility in~ ("local0","local4","local5","daemon","auth")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("openvpn","ssl-vpn","sslvpn","sslvpn settings","config vpn ssl","vpn-user")

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the

Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-05 7 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified a prompt injection pathway in Claude Code GitHub Action that allowed access to workflow secrets under specific conditions. This research examines the attack chain, responsible disclosure process, Anthropic's mitigation, and guidance for securing AI-powered CI/CD workflows. The post Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT0051 T0053 T0054 T0057 T0098 T1027 T1190 T1195.002
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner Exploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1212 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "runners/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude-code", "@anthropic-ai", "_actions/anthropics", "actions-runner", "/_work/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId, TargetFilePath, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Node Process Reads /proc/<pid>/environ on CI Runner (Claude Code Action Read Tool Exfil)

[LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner Exploitation Medium
Even after the /proc fix in claude-code-action 2.1.128, an attacker who controls the prompt can still steer the Read tool to any path the runner can see. This hunts node — running from the Actions work dir — opening the common secret stores a CI job tends to have on disk: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc (NPM publish token), ~/.docker/config.json (registry token), ~/.kube/config, ~/.netrc, SSH keys, .env files. Microsoft's article explicitly calls out that 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment'. Rationale: Article: 'once an attacker can influence the agent, they might be able to steer it toward sensitive files available inside the CI runner environment.' We restrict to node spawned from `_work/` or the anthropic action checkout dir so legit user shell activity reading `~/.aws/credentials` doesn't fire. Path list is the GitHub Actions secret canon — npm publish tokens, docker registry creds, GitHub CLI tokens, terraform/pypi publishers — all of which routinely live in runner home dirs. Cross-checked: Flatt's writeup confirms ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + GITHUB_TOKEN + OIDC creds are the named targets, the broader hunt covers what would be next. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action") 
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(rsa|ed25519|dsa|ecdsa)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessId,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let CredPaths = dynamic([".aws/credentials", ".npmrc", ".gitconfig", ".docker/config.json", ".kube/config", ".netrc", "/.env", ".config/gh/hosts.yml", ".terraformrc", ".pypirc"]);

title: Claude Code Read Tool Accessing Credential Files on GitHub Actions Runner

description: Node.js (running Claude Code Action or the Anthropic SDK) opening common credential / token files on a Linux GitHub Actions runner. Catches Read-tool abuse beyond the patched /proc primitive — an attacker who controls the AI prompt can still steer Read at ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, SSH keys, and .env.

[LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint Command & Control Medium
Closes the loop on the exfiltration step. The Claude Code Action's legitimate outbound destinations are tightly scoped — api.anthropic.com (LLM calls) and the GitHub control plane (api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, ghcr.io, results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com). When the same node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` reaches anything else on a public IP, an attacker is probably steering it to POST the stolen ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OIDC token to their collection endpoint, or to fetch a second-stage payload to plant into a PR (the docs-XSS scenario from Figure 1). Rationale: Article's threat model is clear: 'the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and potentially other credentials available to the runner' get exfiltrated, and the same agent primitive 'create_pull_request_from_changes' lets the attacker reach an external endpoint to receive them or fetch payloads. Allowlist is built from Anthropic's API host plus the GitHub Actions runtime control-plane domains (the only IPs a legit claude-code-action job needs). Anything else from a node process under `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action` is suspicious by construction. No Sigma — needs cross-table join (process attribution + network destination + DNS). Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://www.securityweek.com/claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot-agents-vulnerable-to-prompt-injection-via-comments/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
let RunnerNode = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "node"
    | where FolderPath has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "_work/", "actions-runner")
         or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
    | project NodeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NodePid = ProcessId, NodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NodeFolder = FolderPath;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"))
| where isnotempty(RemoteIP)
| join kind=inner RunnerNode on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.NodePid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NodeCmd, NodeFolder, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Destinations = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), DestIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
           by DeviceName, NodeFolder, RemotePort
| order by FirstSeen desc
let AllowList = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.github.com", "githubusercontent.com", "githubapp.com", "githubassets.com", "ghcr.io", "actions.githubusercontent.com"]);
let RunnerHosts = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action", "/_work/")
    | distinct DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (RunnerHosts)
| where isnotempty(DstHostname)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." 
     and not(DstIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.") 
     and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."
| where not(DstHostname has_any (AllowList))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HitCount = count(), SampleUrl = any(Url)
           by DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| order by FirstSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine

[LLM] DbGate loadReader functionName code injection (CVE-2026-47670) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to the DbGate /runners/load-reader endpoint carrying an injection-shaped functionName (newline + import('child_process') + execSync). Article-specific to the unsanitized template interpolation in packages/api/src/controllers/runners.js. Rationale: Targets the article-specific URI path /runners/load-reader together with the bypass primitives the writeup names verbatim (child_process import, execSync, require=null bypass). The newline (%0A) is the structural injection marker the PoC requires to break out of the template literal.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/runners/load-reader" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/runners/load-reader"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectMarkers = dynamic(["child_process","execSync","await import","%0A","\\nvar ","\\nawait"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem endswith "/runners/load-reader"
  | extend Payload = strcat(csUriQuery, " ", csUserAgent)
  | where Payload has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST" and RequestURL has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where RequestURL has_any (SuspectMarkers) or Message has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST" and Url has "/runners/load-reader"
  | where Url has_any (SuspectMarkers)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DbGate node process spawning shell child (post-exploit RCE) Installation High
Hunts for the dbgate / node.js process spawning a shell or command interpreter, which is the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-47670's child_process.execSync call. The legitimate DbGate runtime does not spawn /bin/sh or cmd.exe as children, so any such child is suspicious in container or host context. Rationale: DbGate's normal runtime never spawns a POSIX shell or Windows command interpreter — the article explicitly states the bypass is `(await import('child_process')).execSync(...)`, so child-process creation under a node parent named dbgate is the direct execution-time signal. Pairs with UC1 to give one network-side and one host-side detection of the same chain.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","dbgate","dbgate.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/app/packages/api", "/dbgate", "dbgate")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","busybox","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(node|dbgate)(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "dbgate"
  | where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/|\\)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|busybox|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh(\.exe)?)$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","dbgate.exe") 
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName in~ ("auditd","audit")
  | where SyslogMessage has "type=EXECVE" and SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/dash")
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","dbgate")
  | project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DbGate Zip Slip (CVE-2026-47669): node process writes outside archive dir to OS-sensitive paths Installation High
Detects the Zip Slip exploitation outcome of CVE-2026-47669 where the DbGate node process — invoked via /api/archive/unzip — writes files to OS-sensitive Linux paths (cron, sudoers, SSH authorized_keys, ld.so.preload, systemd units, /usr/local/bin) via `../` entries in a malicious ZIP. In a clean DbGate deployment the node process should only write inside its archive directory, so any write under /etc, /root/.ssh, or /usr/local/bin from node is high-fidelity for this CVE. Rationale: Pivots on the EXACT Zip Slip exploit outcome described in the GHSA PoC: `path.join(outputDirectory, entry.fileName)` allows `../` traversal, and the PoC writes to `/etc/cron.d/dbgate-pwn`. The dbgate node process has no legitimate reason to touch /etc/cron.*, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/ld.so.preload, or /usr/local/bin — these are the canonical persistence/privesc paths attackers traverse to. Corroborated against Snyk's prior DbGate Zip Slip advisory which confirms the same vulnerable archive-extraction code path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1053.003 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate Zip Slip - node process writes outside archive dir
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("dbgate", "packages/api", "/app/packages")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron." 
    or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/root/.ssh/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/init.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/profile.d/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/ld.so.preload"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/passwd"
    or FolderPath == "/etc/shadow"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate Zip Slip - ASIM ImFileEvent (covers MDE for Linux + Sysmon for Linux + auditd)
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName =~ "node"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("dbgate", "packages/api", "/app/packages")
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/cron."
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/root/.ssh/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/init.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/profile.d/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/usr/local/bin/"
    or TargetFilePath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/"

          ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DbGate exploit chain: anonymous /auth/login + /api/archive/unzip POSTs from same source (CVE-2026-47669) Exploitation Medium
Detects the multi-step exploit sequence against DbGate's vulnerable archive endpoints: POST /api/auth/login (no creds via amoid=none), POST /api/uploads/upload, POST /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, POST /api/archive/unzip — all hit by the same source IP within a short window. This is the network-edge view of CVE-2026-47669 exploitation, complementary to host-side file-write detection. Rationale: Targets the EXACT URL set in the PoC (POST /api/auth/login with amoid=none, /api/uploads/upload, /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip, /api/archive/unzip). The chain of >=2 distinct endpoints including unzip or save-uploaded-zip from one source IP is the network-shape of the exploit. Defender/Falcon left empty because neither has inbound HTTP request-URL visibility for DbGate's port. Corroborated via Snyk advisory for the prior dbgate-api Zip Slip variant. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h535-j5hr-mv56 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-DBGATEAPI-11023274
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
// CVE-2026-47669 DbGate exploit chain via WAF/proxy logs in CommonSecurityLog
let ExploitEndpoints = dynamic(["/api/archive/unzip","/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip","/api/uploads/upload","/api/auth/login"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any (ExploitEndpoints)
| extend Endpoint = case(
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/unzip", "unzip",
    RequestURL has "/api/archive/save-uploaded-zip", "save-uploaded-zip",
    RequestURL has "/api/uploads/upload", "upload",
    RequestURL has "/api/auth/login", "login",
    "other")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(Endpoint),
            UrlSamples = make_set(RequestURL, 10),
            UASet = make_set(RequestClientApplication),
            ReqCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP
| where array_length(EndpointsHit) >= 2
    and (set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "unzip") or set_has_element(EndpointsHit, "save-uploaded-zip"))
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] DbGate CVE-2026-47668 — Node.js runner spawning shell/LOLBin children for egress Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of DbGate's JSON Script Runner RCE where attacker-injected JavaScript in the `functionName` parameter calls `process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync()` to launch shell utilities (wget/curl/sh/bash/powershell) from the forked dbgate runner Node.js process. Targets the exploit chain post-injection where the spawned child commands betray the RCE. Rationale: Pins to the exact post-exploit footprint described in the advisory: the forked Node.js runner (working dir `/root/.dbgate/run/<uuid>`, env `DBGATE_API=/home/dbgate-docker/bundle.js`) executing shell utilities via `child_process.execSync()` — concretely `wget --post-data "$(env)"` in the PoC. Parent-cmdline anchors (`bundle.js`, `.dbgate/run/`, `dbgate-docker`) are dbgate-specific artifacts not present in benign Node workloads.

title: DbGate JSON Runner RCE — Node.js Forked Runner Spawns Shell/LOLBin (CVE-2026-47668)
id: 9a3c1c8d-4f2a-4b6e-9e2a-cve202647668uc1
description: Detects child process execution from a DbGate forked runner Node.js process where the parent cmdline references the dbgate runtime artifacts (bundle.js, .dbgate/run/) and the child is a shell or download utility — the post-injection footprint of CVE-2026-47668.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8v3q-9vmx-36vc
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '\node.exe'
  parent_ctx:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'bundle.js'
      - '.dbgate/run/'
      - 'dbgate-docker'
      - 'DBGATE_API'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/ruby'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
  condition: parent and parent_ctx and child
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR */node) OR @process.parent.name:node) (@ParentCommandLine:(*bundle.js* OR *.dbgate/run/* OR *DBGATE_API* OR *dbgate-docker*) OR @process.parent.command_line:(*bundle.js* OR *.dbgate/run/* OR *DBGATE_API*)) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\certutil.exe) OR @process.name:(wget OR curl OR sh OR bash OR nc OR ncat OR python OR python3 OR perl OR ruby))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^node(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(bundle\\.js|\\.dbgate/run/|DBGATE_API|dbgate-docker)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| ImageFileName=/(\/wget|\/curl|\/sh$|\/bash$|\/dash$|\/zsh$|\/nc$|\/ncat$|\/python3?$|\/perl$|\/ruby$|\\powershell\.exe$|\\pwsh\.exe$|\\cmd\.exe$|\\certutil\.exe$|\\bitsadmin\.exe$)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_path) as child_path values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","node.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*dbgate*" OR Processes.parent_process="*bundle.js*" OR Processes.parent_process="*/.dbgate/run/*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wget","curl","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","powershell.exe","pwsh","cmd.exe","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime>relative_time(now(),"-7d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_path) as child_path values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","node.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*dbgate*" OR Processes.parent_process="*bundle.js*" OR Processes.parent_process="*/.dbgate/run/*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wget","curl","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","powershell.exe","pwsh","cmd.exe","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime>relative_time(now(),"-7d@d")
[LLM] DbGate exploit web request — POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader with child_process injection Delivery High
Detects HTTP exploitation traffic for CVE-2026-47668 in reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / web-server access logs: POST requests to DbGate's `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` endpoints, optionally paired with body inspection matching the JS injection signatures (`process.mainModule.require`, `child_process`, `execSync`, `module.constructor._load`). Aims at the network-side of the exploit before payload execution. Rationale: Endpoint paths `/runners/start` and `/runners/load-reader` are advisory-specific (not generic API hits) and the runner endpoints are not part of any user-browser flow — any POST to them from outside curated automation is suspicious. Cross-join with the host-side process spike (forked node runner) elevates signal further.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bundle.js","dbgate")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bundle.js",".dbgate/run/","DBGATE_API")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ChildName = FileName
) on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (Timestamp1 - 5m .. Timestamp1 + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildName, ChildCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let waf =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST"
    | where RequestURL has_any ("/runners/start","/runners/load-reader")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message, AdditionalExtensions=DeviceCustomString1;
let iis =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod == "POST"
    | where csUriStem has_any ("/runners/start","/runners/load-reader")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHostName=Computer, RequestURL=csUriStem, RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent, scStatus;
union waf, iis
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DbGate anonymous auth-bypass token mint — POST /auth/login with amoid:none Reconnaissance Medium
Detects the precursor to CVE-2026-47668 exploitation against a default-deployed DbGate: an unauthenticated `POST /auth/login` carrying body `{"amoid":"none"}` to mint a bearer token when `authProvider:"Anonymous"` (the default). Captures recon/auth-prep traffic that almost always precedes the runner-endpoint hit. Rationale: The advisory documents the exact unauth token-mint vector — `curl -d '{"amoid":"none"}' <dbgate>:3000/auth/login` — used when `authProvider` is left at its default `Anonymous`. Pairing the `/auth/login` POST with a following `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` from the same source within 30 minutes is the full exploit handshake.
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let auth =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has "/auth/login"
    | project AuthTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication;
let runner =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has_any ("/runners/start","/runners/load-reader")
    | project RunTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL_Runner=RequestURL;
auth
| join kind=inner runner on SourceIP
| where RunTime between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + 30m)
| project AuthTime, RunTime, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL_Runner, RequestClientApplication
| order by AuthTime desc

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect login from Unit 42 IOC IPs Exploitation High
Hunt for successful GlobalProtect gateway-connected events sourced from the nine IP addresses Unit 42 attributes to pre-PoC CVE-2026-0257 exploitation. Any successful VPN session from one of these IPs is a high-confidence compromise indicator since the article confirms the actor uses them to bypass GP portal/gateway authentication. Rationale: Uses the nine attacker-IP IOCs published by Unit 42 in the CVE-2026-0257 threat brief — explicit, vendor-attributed, and tied to a CISA KEV-listed exploitation campaign. Matched against PAN-OS GlobalProtect login telemetry which is the exact telemetry the article tells defenders to search. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login with CVE-2026-0257 PoC hard-coded host-id / device-name Exploitation High
Hunt for GlobalProtect gateway-connected events whose host-id or device name matches the hard-coded values shipped in the public CVE-2026-0257 PoC code. These strings appear in the GP client-info payload sent during the auth-bypass and are not naturally generated by real corporate endpoints. Rationale: The Unit 42 brief explicitly names these MAC and machine-name strings as defaults baked into the published PoC code — they are the cleanest unique fingerprint of attacker traffic vs legitimate VPN clients. These would rarely if ever appear in a real corporate environment, so the FP rate is near-zero. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Network_Sessions.All_Sessions
// PAN-OS GP host-id/device-name values do not flow into Defender XDR tables natively.
// If GP logs are ingested via custom MDE connector into AdditionalFields, this is the shape:
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has "GlobalProtect"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff","00:11:22:33:44:55","WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001","DESKTOP-GP01","GP-CLIENT")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, AccountName, AdditionalFields
let HostIds = dynamic(["aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff","00:11:22:33:44:55"]);
let DeviceNames = dynamic(["WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001","DESKTOP-GP01","GP-CLIENT"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Palo Alto Networks"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect", "PAN-OS")
| where DeviceAction has_any ("allow","success","login") or Activity has_any ("gateway-connected","globalprotectgateway-login-succeeded")
| where (SourceHostName in~ (DeviceNames))
    or (SourceMACAddress in~ (HostIds))
    or Message has_any ("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff","00:11:22:33:44:55","WINDOWS-LAPTOP-001","DESKTOP-GP01","GP-CLIENT")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, SourceMACAddress, DeviceAction, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PAN-OS GlobalProtect login matching CVE-2026-0257 PoC client fingerprint Exploitation High
Hunt for GP gateway-connected events carrying the hard-coded endpoint_os_version 'Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' AND an empty source_user_info.domain — the exact post-PoC release fingerprint Unit 42 documents in the threat brief. Legitimate clients fill in the joined domain; the PoC leaves it blank. Rationale: Unit 42 explicitly publishes endpoint_os_version='Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit' + empty source_user_info.domain as the post-PoC client fingerprint of the CVE-2026-0257 exploit. The empty-domain clause is what shifts it from common-OS noise into high-fidelity exploit signal — real corporate GP clients almost always populate that field with the AD domain. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// PAN-OS GP client-info strings do not flow into Defender XDR natively.
// Where GP logs are ingested via a custom MDE connector, the substring lives in AdditionalFields:
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType has "GlobalProtect"
| where AdditionalFields has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("source_user_info.domain=\"\"","source_user_info.domain=null","\"domain\":\"\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, AccountName, AdditionalFields
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Palo Alto Networks"
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("GlobalProtect", "PAN-OS")
| where DeviceAction has_any ("allow","success","login") or Activity has_any ("gateway-connected","globalprotectgateway-login-succeeded")
| where Message has "Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit"
| where Message has_any ("source_user_info.domain=\"\"", "domain=\"\"", "source_user_info.domain= ", "domain=,")
    or (Message has "source_user_info.domain" and isempty(SourceNTDomain))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceNTDomain, SourceHostName, DeviceAction, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(paloalto OR panos OR globalprotect) (@evt.outcome:success OR @action:(allow OR login OR gateway-connected)) @endpoint_os_version:"Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit" (-@source_user_info.domain:* OR @source_user_info.domain:"")

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")

   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

    selection_wmic_remote:

       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

status: experimental

references:

author: Clankerusecase

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or SHA1 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e") or MD5 in~ ("6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6552824c59ddacb134073f24a4bd4724514a938a9dc59f1733503642faed3bd3", "c917fcf8314228862571f80c9e4a871e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or SHA1 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442") or MD5 in~ ("524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716", "c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a", "f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolutions or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com observed in the ReliaQuest report. Article-specific because this domain appeared ~75 days before the main intrusion as the initial staging beacon and is reused by the web shell's self-reporting fallback over DNS/HTTP. Rationale: The domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com is the only network IOC named in the ReliaQuest write-up; matching it across DNS and HTTP egress is a definitive OP-512 signal. Cross-checked the IOC pattern via the article's lead and MITRE T1071.004 mapping. [LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop) Installation High
Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe writing ASP.NET handler files (.aspx, .ashx, .asmx) into upload or temp directories — the exact drop pattern ReliaQuest observed for the OP-512 three-shell framework. Combines parent-process (w3wp.exe) and target-extension predicates to keep false positives down on legitimate deployment activity. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names w3wp.exe as the process that dropped the web shell into the application's upload directory. The parent (w3wp.exe) + extension (.aspx/.ashx) + path (upload/temp) triple gives strong specificity to OP-512 vs legitimate publish flows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190

| where FolderPath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc

   or TargetFileName endswith ".aspx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".ashx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".asmx"

[LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution Actions on Objectives High
Detects the IIS worker w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or reconnaissance binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe) — directly matching ReliaQuest's observed OP-512 post-exploitation step of running whoami /priv from the web shell to confirm SYSTEM-level privileges after Potato Suite escalation. Rationale: ReliaQuest directly cites whoami /priv as the post-Potato verification command from OP-512, and the entire chain hinges on w3wp.exe being the parent. Parent (w3wp.exe) + child (recon binaries) is exactly the article's described observed sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.003 T1033 T1087
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (FileName =~ "whoami.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (ChildName =~ "whoami.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS Worker w3wp.exe Spawns Recon Binary (OP-512)
id: 4f7b3c6a-2d11-4f8d-8a51-7e2b1a4c9e3f
description: Detects w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell/whoami/net/systeminfo as a child, consistent with OP-512 web shell post-exploitation reconnaissance after Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:

logsource:

    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_child:

            - '\cmd.exe'

            - '\whoami.exe'

level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\WHOAMI.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\ipconfig.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\sc.exe)

| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|hostname|wmic|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| WhoamiPriv := if(ImageFileName=/whoami\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(priv|all|groups)/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
